command.description: Executable for a stdio server. Use `command` or `url`, not both.

description.description: What the server is for, read by drafters choosing tools.

env.description: Environment for a stdio server. Values expand `${NAME}` references.

files.description: How a file reference (`blob:sha256-…`) in a tool call's arguments reaches the server: `path` as a local file path, `url` as a link the server can fetch, `base64` as the file's contents, `off` as the reference text unchanged.

description.description: Replaces the server's description of the tool.

output_example.description: An example of the tool's output.

url.description: Endpoint for a streamable HTTP server.

mcp.description: MCP servers, as `[mcp.<name>]`. Their tools join the catalog as `<name>__<tool>`.

context_window.description: The model's context window in tokens.

description.description: What the role's model is good for, shown to drafters beside the role's name. Standard roles have a built-in one that this replaces; a custom role needs one to be offered through a prompt tool's or `builtin__generate_image`'s `model` input.

fallbacks.description: Models to try, in order, when this one fails.

context_window.description: The model's context window in tokens.

type.description: What the role's model does. Custom roles default to `chat`; standard roles have a fixed type (`decider` is `decision`, `image` is `image`, the rest are `chat`). The role's provider must serve this type.

models.description: Model roles, as `[models.<role>]`. Standard roles are `default`, `chat`, `drafter`, `planner`, `outliner`, `solver`, `repair`, `judge`, `decider` and `image`; any other name is a custom role.

exclude.description: Glob patterns over `<kind>__<item>` for items only the pack's own plans and agents can call.

git.description: The git repository the pack is installed from.

include.description: Glob patterns over `<kind>__<item>`, such as `plan__*`, naming the items callable from outside the pack. Everything when empty.

path.description: The pack's directory inside the repository, such as `github`. Its releases are the tags `<path>/vX.Y.Z`. The repository root when absent.

ref.description: The release line (`v1`), exact release (`v1.2.0`) or branch to install. Release refs name the pack's own version; dive adds the `<path>/` tag prefix.

packs.description: Installed packs, as `[packs.<name>]`. Their tools, plans and agents join the catalog as `<name>__<kind>__<item>`.

output_image.description: Output image tokens. Defaults to the `output` rate.

source.description: Where the price came from. The desktop app writes `models.dev` when it fills a price from the [models.dev](https://models.dev) catalogue, refreshes only prices marked that way, and drops the mark when you edit one by hand.

tiers.description: Higher rates for a call whose prompt is over a token count, as `[[pricing."<model>".tiers]]`. The prompt counts input, cache-write and cache-read tokens. The highest tier the prompt passes prices every token of the call. A tier's missing output rate keeps the base rate; its missing cache rates scale with its input rate.

above.description: The tier applies when the prompt has more tokens than this.

pricing.description: Prices per model id, as `[pricing."<model>"]`, in USD per million tokens. Without them, usage is reported in tokens only.

project.description: This project's identity. Belongs in the project config.

id.description: An id Dive generates the first time you store a project secret with `dive secret set NAME --project`. Project secrets are keyed by it, so renaming or moving the folder keeps them. Letters, digits and hyphens.

prompts.description: Deprecated. Customize agents with agent files instead.

api_key.description: API key, usually a `${NAME}` reference to a variable or stored secret.

profile.description: Credentials profile, where the provider uses one.

region.description: Cloud region, where the provider needs one.

type.description: The provider. `systemone` serves decision models, `gemini` serves image models (the Gemini API), and the rest serve chat models.

data_dir.description: Where threads and the shape cache are stored.

history_limit.description: Most past messages sent with each turn.

max_agent_iterations.description: Most model rounds a conversation agent takes in one turn.

planning_attempts.description: Attempts the built-in planner gets before giving up.

backend.description: `memory` keeps nothing between runs. `DIVE_STORAGE` overrides it.

files.description: Where files that tools return, such as screenshots, are kept. Omitted, files follow `backend`: under `<data_dir>/files`, or in memory.

access_key_id.description: The access key ID. Expands `${NAME}` references.

backend.description: `file` keeps files under `<data_dir>/files`, `memory` keeps nothing between runs, and `s3` uses an S3 or S3-compatible bucket.

bucket.description: The bucket to keep files in. Required for `s3`.

endpoint.description: The S3 endpoint URL, for S3-compatible servers such as Garage or MinIO. Omitted means AWS.

prefix.description: A key prefix inside the bucket, so several stores can share one.

region.description: The bucket's region. S3-compatible servers often use their own name, such as `garage`.

secret_access_key.description: The secret access key. Expands `${NAME}` references.

capture_content.description: Include prompts and responses in spans.

endpoint.description: The OTLP/HTTP endpoint. Telemetry is off without one.

headers.description: Headers sent with every export, such as auth.

logs.description: Export logs as well as traces.

always_loaded.description: Tools offered up front, never deferred behind a search. Plan drafting always offers them, and an agent gets the ones its `tools` list matches.

context.description: Anything agents should know about you.

version.description: The file version the config is written in. Omitted means 1; `dive config migrate` brings a file to the current version.

log_path.description: Where the workbench writes its log. Defaults to `<data_dir>/workbench.log`; `DIVE_WORKBENCH_LOG` overrides it.

variables.description: How Dive reports progress and failures on stderr. Unset, stderr is for people.
variables.name: DIVE_EVENTS

values.github: A failing `dive plan run` also prints a `::error::` annotation to stdout, which GitHub Actions shows on the run.
values.jsonl: stderr becomes a stream of JSON events, one per line. `ask` steps can't prompt anyone, so they use their `whenUnanswered` setting.

variables.description: A log filter for stderr, such as `info` or `dive_core=debug`. `-v`, `-vv` and `-vvv` set `info`, `debug` and `trace`.
variables.name: DIVE_LOG

x-environment.description: `${NAME}` references in config.toml and in tool `env` values read the environment variable `NAME` first, then the OS credential store: this project's entry, then the one every project shares. See [Secret references](/reference/configuration#secret-references).

variables.description: Whether `${NAME}` references read the OS credential store when the environment doesn't set `NAME`.
variables.name: DIVE_SECRET_STORE

values.os: Read the macOS Keychain, or the Secret Service on Linux, under service `dive`. Where neither is available, Dive reads the environment only.

variables.description: Where Dive keeps threads and the shape cache.
variables.name: DIVE_STORAGE

values.memory: In memory only. Nothing is kept between runs.

variables.description: Where the workbench writes its log.
variables.name: DIVE_WORKBENCH_LOG

variables.description: The OTLP/HTTP endpoint to export to.
variables.name: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT

variables.description: Extra headers as comma-separated `key=value` pairs, added to the configured ones.
variables.name: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS

x-sections.body:
A string value can include `${NAME}` references, such as `api_key = "${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}"`. Each reference reads the environment variable `NAME`. When `NAME` isn't set, or is set but empty, Dive reads the OS credential store instead: the macOS Keychain, or the Secret Service on Linux, under service `dive` and account `NAME`. The value is resolved each time a config file loads and is never written to a file. Store a value with `dive secret set NAME`. On macOS the Keychain lets only the program that stored a value read it, so `dive secret set` replaces a value another program stored, such as Loon Dive or a different `dive` build, and that program then can't read it until it stores the value again. See every name the config, tools and packs reference, and where each resolves from, with `dive secret list`.

A name neither source has leaves a provider or MCP server loadable, and using that provider or server fails naming the variable. A missing name anywhere else fails the load.

Where no credential store is available, as in a container or on Linux without a Secret Service daemon, Dive reads the environment only. Set `DIVE_SECRET_STORE` to `none` to skip the store on purpose.
